cells.remarks: Issued from Kaliṅganagara. Records the gift, in perpetuity, by the Yuvarāja of the village of Nāmpalli in the Niḍijēru viṣhaya, freed from all taxes and imposts, for the spiritual merit of the donor and his parents. The donee was Sāmījīja, the son of Guṇamārāja, an ornament of the Ayanakula. The grant was composed by Mahāsāndhivigrahi Raha śrī-Sāmanta and engraved by śrī-Dāma- chandra. Published in Journal of Oriental Research, Madras, Volume IX, pp. 59 ff. and plates.

BOLLEPALIN.—Pillar set up in front of the Śiva temple.
cells.date: Jagadekamalla year 10, Prabhava, Vaiśākha śu. Akshatriya, Saturday = 1147 A.D., April 5.
cells.remarks: Records the consecration of Śrī Mailāradeva in the [dha]valāra constructed by the donor in a garden east of the village Inta near Bollepalli under Bhuvanagiri and gift of money for offerings to the deity by Médayabhaṭṭu, son of Saudara Mallenāyaka-Birudānāyaka of Podatūru and Bollanamma and the grandson of Médaya-bhaṭṭu of Bhāradvāja-gotra, described as the lord of Kollipuramu in Vengi-nāḍu. It also records some gift of lands to the same deity by the donor's father. Contra. Bhāratī, Vol. 46, part 3, pp. 5 ff.

cells.remarks: Records the grant of the village Kroṭṭapalli by Gaṅgāyava-maṇḍalēśa to Munindrādhāmāyati, a disciple of Pāṇipātra-prabhu for worship and offerings of the three deities, Sāraṅgi, Nṛsiṁha and Daityasūda and also for the feeding of the yatis residing at Mēkhala for the merit of himself and his parents. The genealogy of Gaṅgayava is given as in Nos. 3 and 10 above. It also describes the tīrthas like Mēkhala, Śuka and Sukla where the above three deities are stated to have been housed. It also records the gift of 48 nishkas to the deities Nṛsiṁha and Sāraṅgi and 12 nishkas to Daityasūdanadēva and 60 nishkas for feeding the inhabitants of the tīrtha, annually.

cells.remarks: Records the construction of a tank at Yēānpūru by Bātēja, a servant of the chief who is described as the son-in-law of Kutubana-Maluka ruling the Nallagonda under the authority of Yēruva-simhāsanamu, for the benefit of himself and his overlord. cells.place: L.D. Institute of Indology. Pedestal of a bronze image. Findspot : Not known.
cells.remarks: The text, made up of one verse in the Śragdharā metre, states that the merchant chief (śreṣṭhi-mukhyah) Durggaka, belonging to the Vidyādhara-gachchha, accompanied probably by his wife Shasthhavvā, constructed a temple (bhavana), for the Tīrthēśvaras and also got excavated a huge tank for purposes of bathing. The writing on the right and left sides of the pedestal registers the obeisance of Durgga-mahattara and Shasthhabhā. The characters, which are cursive, belong to the 8th-9th century A.D.

cells.location: VONṆŪR
cells.place: Slab kept outside the Prabhudēva temple. No. 1.
cells.date: Chālukya Vikrama [3]8, Jaya, Śrāvaṇa śu. 5, Sunday, Uttarāyaṇa-saṅkrānti. Irregular.
cells.remarks: Refers to the king's feudatory Mahāmaṇḍalēśvara Kumāra Jayasiṅgadhēva as governing Kūṇḍi-Three thousand. States that at the request of Chōladēva and all the nāḍaprabhugavaṇḍas and nāḍagāvuṇḍas at his capital Jayantipura, Kumāra Jayasiṅgadēva, after laying the feet of the Kālamukha teacher Bāla-chandrapaṇḍitēva, at Āchārya of Hariharādityadēva, at Oṇanūr in Kundurgge-70, caused the installation of the eight liṅgas of Jayasiṅghēśvara (temple). Registers a grant of land for the worship of the deity for feeding the ascetics and for the purpose of imparting education probably the Brāhmaṇa-gāvuṇḍa of the place. Also records the gift of a village by name Bennekuppe . for the renovation (of the temple) and for rearing a flower-garden. States that the record is the composition (barepam) of Kaṇṇōja, son of Jōgōja of Mūlavalli, described as a devotee of Sarasvati.

cells.remarks: The inscription is in three parts. Noticed in Ep. Ind., Vol. XXXI, p. 30.

cells.place:
GREATER BOMBAY DISTRICT
BOMBAY CITY TALUK
BOMBAY.-Hero-stone deposi-
ted in the Prince of Wales
Museum. Findspot : Maṇṭūr,
Hubli Taluk, Dharwar District,
Karnataka. Impressions recei-
ved from Shri B.V. Shetti.
cells.remarks: Records that it (the sculptured slab) was made by Kalkuṭṭiga Konna and was caused to be made by one (name not clear). Contains the epithets like Kaḍugali-sēva, sabhbha (sarva) satyanirantara and ammana vattiga. Men- tions one Goṇaruppa (Guṇarūpa) probably the hero in whose memory the stone was set up. Appears to state that some one followed the deceased person in death. At the lower portion of the slab are carved the symbols of the ashamaṅgala. In characters of about the 8th century.

cells.place:
KANYAKUMARI DISTRICT —Concld.
KALKULAM TALUK
TIRUNANDIKKARA (Sub-village of TRIPPARAPPU). — Rock-cut Nandīśvara temple, pillar in the front maṇḍapa.
cells.remarks: Records that in the year expressed as [Talai-kkaļait-tuk-kaļam-agav-āṇḍu, the perumakkal of Tirunandikkarai and the administrator of the temple (tafiyalyāṇ) assembled at Kuruṇdambākkam, probably renamed that place as Nandimangalam and donated it to Nambi Kaṇavati for meeting certain expenses of the mid-night worship of the god of the temple. In characters of the 9th century A.D. Cf. T. A. S., Vol. III, pp. 202 ff.

cells.place: West wall in the same place.
cells.remarks: Damaged partly. Commences with the king's praśasti, Tirumagal pōla etc. Records that the village Muṭṭam in the Vaḷḷuva-nādu, a sub-division of Rājarājatteṇgāḍu was renamed as Mummuḍiśoḻanallūr and was granted to the god Tirunandikkarai-Mādēva in the same nādu for conducting a seven-day festival of the god in the month of Aippigai (i.e., Aippaśi) probably ending with bathing ceremony of the idol on the day of Sadayam, the natal star of the king, and for burning a perpetual lamp named as Rājarājan. Other details are lost. Cf. ibid., Vol. I, p. 292, and plate.

cells.date: Regnal year 12, Mithuna 12, śu.. Maghā, ...... · Sunday, Irregular.
cells.remarks: gandar to the god of the temple Alaga-pperumāḷ-vippagar situated to the west of the same locality. Āḍan-Eri and Gaṅgakular-dēvanallūr alias Ālaṇpiganda[sō]lachaturvēdi-maṅgalam are mentioned among the boundaries of the gift land. Fragmentary. Records the declaration by the ūr of the village, Śūluṁ-araśar-gaṇḍan in Śuravī- nāḍu conferring (1) on the god Alagapperumāḷ-vippanagar-Emberumānāg the right to the revenue from two taxes (viz. kaḍamai and antarāyam) from the village Pagaiyāpēri alias Alagapperumānallūr, kuḍikkāḍu on the southern side of their village ; and (2) on Rājāṅgadh Māṇikkachchokkan, a kaikōlā residing in Madurai, the right of cultivating the same. The lands that had been gifted to some god by the said Māṇikkachchokkan in the same locality was excluded from the transaction. The linear measure Kuḍi-rāṅgi-padi-nē[r]ikkol is mentioned.

cells.place: Kallappiran temple, stone built into the east wall of the maṇḍapa.
cells.remarks: Beginning broken and lost. Commences with the king's eulogy Tirumaṅgalpōla, etc. Records a gift of 13 mā of land, by purchase, and certain vessels (weights specified) made of bell-metal, by Ādiṟai niṟāḍi alias Parakēsari-mūvēndaveḻan of Uṟu[kkāḍu] in Avūrk-kūṟgam on the southern bank of the Kāvēri in Sōṇāḍu for burning two perpetual lamps in the temple of Emperumān in Śrīvaikuṇṭam, a dēvadāna in Varaguṇamaṅgalam, a brahmadēya in Tiruvaluḍivalanāḍu and for feeding (uttamagrām) daily 10 brāhmaṇas well-versed in the vēdas and śāstras coming from outside at the time of food-offerings to the god during the mid-day worship. The mahāsabhai of Varaguṇamaṅgalam exempted the land from taxes. Part of this inscription engraved on another stone is noticed. (A.R.Ep., 1959-60, No. B 372).

cells.remarks: Contains a string of epithets of Hiravijaya sūri of the Tapā-gachchha including the one referring to his having been honoured by the emperor, who is stated to have died by starvation (anasāna), at Unnatadurgam on the first date. cells.remarks: Records that Sāṁº Thādārū, son of Sāº Śrīmalla, a Bhaṇḍādīka (store-keeper) and his wife belonging to Upakēśa-vaṁśa and inhabitants of Jēsalamēru (Jaisalmer), with their sons Hurarāja and Mēgharāja caused to be made a place for or with the pādukas (i.e. foot prints) of the 1452 Gaṇadharas, beginning with Puṇḍarīka and ending with Gautama for the increase of the merit (evidently for them). This was consecrated by Jinarāja-sūri of the Kharataragachchha. ibid., p. 68, No. XXVI.

cells.location: RĀJUPĒTA
cells.place: Slab over the tank bund. (impression from the Chief Epigraphist, Archaeological Survey of India, Mysore).
cells.remarks: States that the tank of the village Yampūr was constructed during the time of the chief (who is spoken of as His Lordship Masnad-i-‘Ālī Ulugh A‘ẓam Malik Quṭbu 'l-Mulk) by Bābā Khān, a retainer of the greatest of the Maliks, Malik Qiwāmu'l-Mulk. Further states that the builder had sought assistance from the masters and obtained guarantee (gaul) that of the crop grown in the neighbourhood of the tank, one share will be given to the state (Dīwān), two were to be used for the public welfare, and one for the builder who had taken pains and spent his personal money over the construction. The builder also dedicated his share to the langar (i.e. free-kitchen) of the Twelve Imāms. Also states that he obtained on free-hold lease that much land below the tank in which 5 kuṛe seeds could be sown with the intention that the produce therefrom would be utilised for the repairs of the bridge. Ends with an imprecation against those seeking to violate the above provise.

cells.place: Gate known as Phūṭa-Darwāza. Slab on the right jamb
cells.remarks: States that Shāh Jahān left for eastern India on the first date (during the reign of Jahāngīr) leaving Asīr fort in the charge of Rāja Gopāl Dās Gaur who successfully resisted for two years the attack of Sulṭān Parwīz and Mahābat Khān. The Rāja came down and paid obeisance to the king (then Prince Khurram) on his return and was favoured with a rank of 5000, 5000 horse. After some time, the Rāja accompanied the king to Thatta, where he was killed along with his elder son Kunwar Balrām. Shāh Jahān ascended the throne on the second date. Finally, another son of Rāja Māndhāta Manohar Dās Gaur, who was given sole custody of the fort on the third date constructed this gateway in the following year. Published in Ep. Ind. Mos., 1925-26, p. 7 pl. IV (b).

cells.location: RANTHAMBHORE
cells.place: Fort. Slab fixed near the footsteps towards the right side of the ruined mosque.
cells.remarks: Bilingual. Damaged. Purports that Rāja-i-Rājāh Nawwāb Rāja Jagannāthju, his deputy (Nā’ib) the great Khwāja Bhogīndra Singh, the S(Sh)iqdār Raṇā Chauṇḍāju and Miyā Burhān, the Kotwāl of the fort of Ranthambhore, ordered that goods and effects of the Baitu'l-Māl and Paṭāl-Bhog were exempted from levy. Further exhorts that no levy should be charged henceforth. Ends with an imprecation. The stone-cutter (Sang-Tarāsh) was Mādhū (Mādhav). For the Nāgarī version, see No. 136 of Appendix B.
